existingBehavior.DeliveryAssessment: Currently labels AI results as suggestion supported/changes/insufficient evidence, displays locked source and source citations, and offers a scope_clarification draft for unresolved source-label role aliases.
existingBehavior.DeliveryOverview: Already separates system rule mismatches, AI suggestions and human confirmation. Do not create a total score or duplicate immutable version evidence.
existingBehavior.currentBoundary: The buyer creates/reviews requirements; the seller supplies files. Current delivery replacement invalidates stale evidence. Acceptance and payment are separate actions.

uiPlan.sharedIntegrationOwner: Root wires app/page.tsx and DeliveryAssessment.tsx; this slice does not edit those files.
uiPlan.domainOwner: External agent owns final shared decision types, actual server authorization, immutable proposal records, explicit independent buyer/seller confirmation and conservative recheck integration.
uiPlan.layout: One compact left-aligned panel per inspected requirement. Use existing green/cream/ochre palette and inherited typography, small spacing, wrapping filenames and one current primary action. No animation or new global layout.
uiPlan.result: Separate current fact/suggestion/human status by evidence layer. A supported source fact never becomes accepted delivery or a working backend.
uiPlan.nextActor: Name buyer, seller or both and what to supply. For storage unknown, seller supplies actual execution and independently readable stored-record evidence; buyer checks it. Scope unknown asks both to confirm the exact target first.
uiPlan.proposal: Preserve the complete locked source. Choose an uploaded HTML file and optionally a declared form id from parser-provided candidates. No user JSON, CSS selector, API key or SHA input. Parser candidates are declarations, not model guesses, visibility or runtime proof.
uiPlan.confirmation: Show the exact current proposal and each party's explicit saved confirmation. Selecting a file is not proposing it, proposing it is not either party's confirmation, and one party cannot confirm for the other. Revised proposals must not inherit confirmation from a different proposal.
uiPlan.recheck: After a current server-validated two-party agreement, expose an explicit return-to-this-criterion check action. Do not run AI, upload files, save feedback, accept, authorize or pay automatically. Replacement-delivery or historical context is read-only/stale until the server returns a current decision.
uiPlan.errors: Pending saves disable incompatible actions; preserve user selections on a failed request when still in the same context. Delivery/criterion/proposal changes cancel stale async completion and reset or key local draft state. Error messages state what was not saved and ask to reload current records when needed.
uiPlan.reviewLimits: SSR and callback tests prove rendered text/actions and call identity only. Root must separately test actual role authorization, persistence, stale-response handling and desktop/mobile CUA. Human participants remain zero.

syntheticCases.expect: A source-correct AUD18 item and Name/Email evidence keep their own scope; no implicit acceptance.
AUD28 for beef noodles does not pass using AUD18 from tea or another page; buyer can inspect and request seller correction.
Another page or neighboring field/form cannot witness the target relationship; no guessed target is preselected as authority.
Static enquiry/booking markup cannot prove storage or email. Show unknown, seller evidence next, buyer review after it.
Both real parties must explicitly confirm the same current proposal; one party, stale proposal, failed save, or revision is not agreement.
The new delivery cannot silently use old confirmation or evidence; old/new same-criterion history remains available through existing UI.
Confirmed scope exposes an explicit criterion-specific recheck entry; no effect runs on render or confirmation.
Buyer manually requests changes/evidence or accepts only through existing explicit controls; no scope or AI action triggers payment.
